prompt_text: My roof has hail damage in Denver. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you specific, vetted roofing contractors — I just need your Denver neighborhood or ZIP code. If you want names right away, please share that. 

While you decide, here’s what I recommend you do and who to call (types of companies) and why — plus what to ask and warning signs.

Which specific kinds of roofers to call (and why)
- A local, storm-experienced residential roofer — they know Denver weather, local permit rules, and common hail damage patterns. They’ll give the most accurate repair/replace estimate.
- A roofing company experienced with insurance claims and storm restoration — they can help document damage for your insurer, provide the right scope of work, and often work directly with adjusters.
- A manufacturer-certified installer (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, etc.) — certification means they meet installer training standards and can offer extended product warranties.
- One national or regional firm with a Denver office (if you prefer) — larger firms sometimes have more capacity during storm surges and established insurance workflows.

How many to call
- Get at least three written estimates (one local independent, one certified installer, one experienced storm-restoration team). Comparing three helps prevent overcharging and reveals scope differences.

What to verify before you hire
- Current insurance (liability and workers’ comp) — ask for copies.
- Local references and recent storm-job photos.
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF, CertainTeed, etc.) and warranties available.
- Business license/registration and BBB/Google review history.
- Whether they pull permits and inspect/repair roof decking (important after hail).
- Written contract with scope, materials, replacement vs repair details, timeline, payment schedule, and lien waivers.

Key questions to ask when you call
- Do you have experience with hail claims in Denver? Can you provide references from recent hail-damage jobs?
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see certificates?
- Are you a certified installer for any shingle manufacturers?
- Will you tarp or board up immediately if needed? Is emergency work included in the estimate?
- Do you handle insurance paperwork and meet with the adjuster?
- What’s included in the warranty (materials vs labor) and length?
- Do you obtain permits and arrange inspections?

Red flags / things to avoid
- Knock-on-the-door “storm chasers” who pressure you to sign immediately or demand large up-front cash.
- No written estimate or contracts with vague language.
- Requests to have checks made out to the contractor rather than you (your insurer will usually have guidance).
- Extremely low bids with no itemized scope — could be cutting corners.
- Unwillingness to provide proof of insurance or references.

Immediate steps you should take right now
- Photograph all damage from several angles (close-ups and wider shots), date them, and keep receipts for any temporary repairs or tarps.
- Call your insurance company to start a claim — they’ll tell you next steps.
- If there are active leaks, arrange temporary tarping immediately; ask any roofer you call if emergency tarping is available.

If you want, I’ll look up 3–5 vetted roofing contractors in your specific Denver ZIP (I’ll check reviews, certifications, storm experience, and contact info). Tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and I’ll pull those names and short reasons to call each.
